description: Build an annotated phylogenetic tree from sequence data through alignment, model selection, tree inference, support assessment, rooting, and taxonomic reconciliation.

steps.description: Align a set of homologous sequences using a multiple sequence alignment algorithm, then trim poorly aligned regions.

inputs.name: raw-sequences
inputs.desc: FASTA file or sequence set to align

inputs.name: alignment-method
inputs.desc: Algorithm choice (MUSCLE, MAFFT, ClustalW, or T-Coffee)

inputs.name: trimming-threshold
inputs.desc: Gap fraction above which columns are removed

outputs.name: aligned-sequences
outputs.desc: Trimmed multiple sequence alignment

outputs.name: alignment-statistics
outputs.desc: Column count, gap fraction, conserved sites, informative sites

process: Run the chosen alignment algorithm on the raw sequences.
Score each alignment column for gap fraction and conservation.
Trim columns exceeding the gap threshold.
Report alignment length, informative site count, and average pairwise identity.

steps.description: Evaluate candidate nucleotide or amino acid substitution models and select the best fit using information criteria.

outputs.name: selected-model
outputs.desc: Best-fit substitution model with parameters

outputs.name: model-comparison-table
outputs.desc: AIC, BIC, and log-likelihood for each candidate model

process: Enumerate candidate models appropriate to the data type (e.g., JC, HKY, GTR for nucleotides).
Fit each model to the alignment and compute log-likelihood.
Rank models by AIC and BIC.
Select the model with the lowest information criterion score.

steps.description: Infer a phylogenetic tree using maximum likelihood or Bayesian methods under the selected substitution model.

outputs.name: inferred-tree
outputs.desc: Newick-format tree topology with branch lengths

outputs.name: inference-log
outputs.desc: Convergence diagnostics, run time, and likelihood scores

process: Configure the tree search with the selected model and inference method.
Run the analysis (ML heuristic search or MCMC chain).
Check convergence (likelihood plateau for ML, ESS and trace plots for Bayesian).
Extract the best tree (highest likelihood or majority-rule consensus).

steps.description: Assess confidence in each branch of the inferred tree using bootstrap resampling or posterior probabilities.

inputs.name: inferred-tree
inputs.desc: Newick-format tree from the inference step

inputs.name: support-method
inputs.desc: Bootstrap replicates count or Bayesian posterior source

outputs.name: supported-tree
outputs.desc: Tree with support values annotated on each internal node

outputs.name: support-summary
outputs.desc: Distribution of support values and count of well-supported nodes

process: Generate bootstrap replicates or extract posterior tree sample.
Map support values onto each internal node of the best tree.
Classify nodes as well-supported (above threshold) or weakly supported.
Summarize the overall support distribution.

steps.description: Root the phylogenetic tree using an outgroup, midpoint method, or molecular clock assumption.

inputs.name: rooting-method
inputs.desc: Outgroup taxon, midpoint, or molecular clock

outputs.name: rooted-tree
outputs.desc: Rooted tree with directional branch lengths

outputs.name: rooting-rationale
outputs.desc: Justification for the chosen root placement

process: Identify the outgroup or apply the midpoint/clock criterion.
Insert the root at the selected position.
Recalculate branch lengths from the root.
Document why this rooting is appropriate for the dataset.

steps.description: Compare the inferred tree topology against the accepted taxonomy and flag conflicts or novel groupings.

inputs.name: reference-taxonomy
inputs.desc: Accepted taxonomic classification for the included taxa

outputs.name: reconciliation-report
outputs.desc: List of agreements, conflicts, and novel clades relative to accepted taxonomy

outputs.name: annotated-tree
outputs.desc: Tree with taxonomic labels and conflict markers

process: Map each tip label to its accepted taxonomic hierarchy.
Check whether each clade in the tree matches a named taxonomic group.
Flag paraphyletic or polyphyletic groups.
List novel groupings not present in the reference taxonomy.

steps.description: Produce the final annotated phylogeny figure with support values, taxonomic labels, scale bar, and legend.

inputs.name: annotated-tree
inputs.desc: Tree with taxonomic and support annotations

outputs.name: phylogeny-figure
outputs.desc: Publication-ready tree figure with all annotations

outputs.name: phylogeny-report
outputs.desc: Summary of methods, model, support, and taxonomic findings

process: Render the tree with branch lengths proportional to substitutions per site.
Add support values, taxonomic color coding, and conflict markers.
Include a scale bar and legend.
Write the methods and results summary for the phylogeny report.

description: Extract frequency content from a raw signal through windowing, spectral transformation, peak identification, model fitting, and feature quantification.

steps.description: Load and inspect the raw time-series or spectral data, checking sample rate, duration, and obvious artifacts.

inputs.name: raw-data-source
inputs.desc: File path or instrument connection for the raw signal

outputs.name: raw-signal
outputs.desc: Loaded time-series array with timestamps

outputs.name: acquisition-report
outputs.desc: Actual sample rate, duration, gaps, and artifact flags

process: Load the raw data and extract the time and amplitude arrays.
Verify the actual sample rate against the expected value.
Scan for gaps, clipping, or saturation artifacts.
Report signal duration, point count, and any quality issues.

steps.description: Apply a windowing function to the signal to reduce spectral leakage before transformation.

inputs.name: window-type
inputs.desc: Window function (Hann, Hamming, Blackman, Kaiser, or rectangular)

outputs.name: windowed-signal
outputs.desc: Signal after applying the window function

outputs.name: window-parameters
outputs.desc: Window type, length, and equivalent noise bandwidth

process: Select the window function based on the analysis goals (frequency resolution vs. sidelobe suppression).
Apply the window to the signal segment.
Record the equivalent noise bandwidth for amplitude correction.
Optionally segment the signal for averaged periodograms.

steps.description: Compute the frequency-domain representation using FFT, wavelet transform, or Lomb-Scargle periodogram for unevenly sampled data.

outputs.name: spectrum
outputs.desc: Frequency vs. power or amplitude array

outputs.name: transform-metadata
outputs.desc: Frequency resolution, Nyquist frequency, and transform parameters

process: Apply the selected transform to each windowed segment.
Correct amplitudes for the window function's energy loss.
Average across segments if using Welch's method.
Record the frequency resolution and Nyquist limit.

steps.description: Detect peaks in the spectrum, distinguish real peaks from noise floor, and catalog their frequencies and amplitudes.

inputs.name: noise-floor-method
inputs.desc: Method to estimate noise (median, percentile, or modeled)

outputs.name: peak-list
outputs.desc: Table of detected peaks with frequency, amplitude, and SNR

outputs.name: noise-floor-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated noise power spectral density across the band

process: Estimate the noise floor using the selected method.
Identify local maxima exceeding a threshold above the noise floor.
Compute the signal-to-noise ratio for each candidate peak.
Filter out peaks below the minimum SNR criterion.

steps.description: Fit analytical models (Gaussian, Lorentzian, Voigt) to each identified peak and extract center frequency, width, and area.

inputs.name: peak-list
inputs.desc: Table of detected peaks with initial frequency and amplitude

outputs.name: fitted-peaks
outputs.desc: Table of peaks with fitted center, width, area, and goodness of fit

outputs.name: residual-spectrum
outputs.desc: Spectrum minus all fitted peak models

process: Select a peak shape model appropriate to the physical process.
Fit each peak using nonlinear least squares with initial guesses from the peak list.
Record center frequency, FWHM, integrated area, and chi-squared for each fit.
Subtract all fitted peaks from the spectrum to produce the residual.

steps.description: Compute summary metrics from the spectrum: total power, band ratios, harmonic relationships, and spectral slope.

outputs.name: spectral-features
outputs.desc: Table of computed features (total power, band ratios, slopes, harmonic indices)

outputs.name: feature-interpretation
outputs.desc: Brief interpretation of each feature in context

process: Integrate total power across the full band and within defined sub-bands.
Compute ratios between sub-bands.
Check for harmonic relationships among fitted peaks.
Fit a power-law or other trend to the spectral envelope.

steps.description: Produce the spectral analysis report with annotated spectrum plots, peak table, feature summary, and methods description.

outputs.name: spectral-report
outputs.desc: Complete spectral analysis report with figures and tables

outputs.name: spectral-figures
outputs.desc: Annotated spectrum, peak fits, and feature plots

process: Generate the annotated spectrum plot with peak labels and noise floor.
Build the peak parameter table and feature summary table.
Write the methods section covering acquisition, windowing, transform, and fitting.
Compile the figures, tables, and narrative into the final report.

description: Analyze spatially distributed data through coordinate projection, autocorrelation testing, interpolation, layer overlay, hotspot detection, and spatial validation.

steps.description: Import spatial data, assign or verify the coordinate reference system, and project to a common CRS for analysis.

inputs.name: spatial-data-files
inputs.desc: Shapefiles, GeoJSON, CSV with lat/lon, or raster files

outputs.name: projected-data
outputs.desc: All layers in the common CRS

outputs.name: projection-log
outputs.desc: Original CRS, transformations applied, and any datum shift warnings

process: Read each spatial data source and identify its native CRS.
Reproject all layers to the target CRS.
Check for datum shift issues and log any warnings.
Verify that projected coordinates fall within the expected study area bounds.

steps.description: Test whether the observed spatial pattern is clustered, dispersed, or random using Moran's I and local indicators.

inputs.name: projected-data
inputs.desc: Point or polygon data with attribute values in the common CRS

inputs.name: spatial-weights
inputs.desc: Neighborhood definition (distance band, k-nearest, or contiguity)

outputs.name: global-autocorrelation
outputs.desc: Moran's I statistic, expected value, z-score, and p-value

outputs.name: local-indicators
outputs.desc: LISA cluster map classifying each observation as HH, LL, HL, LH, or not significant

process: Construct the spatial weights matrix from the neighborhood definition.
Compute global Moran's I and test significance via permutation.
Compute local Moran's I (LISA) for each observation.
Classify each observation into cluster type and flag significant ones.

steps.description: Estimate values at unsampled locations using kriging, inverse distance weighting, or spline interpolation.

inputs.name: projected-data
inputs.desc: Sample point data with measured values

inputs.name: prediction-grid
inputs.desc: Grid resolution and extent for output surface

outputs.name: interpolated-surface
outputs.desc: Raster of predicted values across the study area

outputs.name: prediction-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Kriging variance or cross-validation error map

process: Fit the variogram model (for kriging) or set the IDW power parameter.
Generate predictions at each grid cell.
Compute prediction uncertainty at each cell.
Run leave-one-out cross-validation and report RMSE.

steps.description: Overlay the interpolated surface with contextual layers (land use, elevation, infrastructure) and extract co-located attributes.

inputs.name: context-layers
inputs.desc: Additional spatial layers for overlay (land use, DEM, boundaries)

outputs.name: enriched-surface
outputs.desc: Raster or table with predicted values plus contextual attributes at each cell

outputs.name: overlay-summary
outputs.desc: Zonal statistics of predicted values within each contextual category

process: Align all layers to the same grid and extent.
Extract contextual attribute values at each prediction cell.
Compute zonal statistics (mean, median, range) within each category.
Flag cells where context suggests the prediction may be unreliable.

steps.description: Identify statistically significant clusters of high and low values using Getis-Ord Gi* or kernel density estimation.

inputs.name: hotspot-method
inputs.desc: Getis-Ord Gi*, kernel density, or DBSCAN

outputs.name: hotspot-map
outputs.desc: Map of statistically significant hot and cold spots

outputs.name: hotspot-table
outputs.desc: Table of hotspot locations with z-scores and p-values

process: Apply the selected hotspot detection method.
Correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni or FDR).
Classify each location as hot spot, cold spot, or not significant.
Tabulate the significant clusters with their spatial extent.

steps.description: Validate the spatial analysis using holdout sample points and compare predicted vs. observed values.

inputs.name: holdout-points
inputs.desc: Withheld sample locations with known values

outputs.name: validation-metrics
outputs.desc: RMSE, MAE, R-squared, and bias at holdout points

outputs.name: residual-map
outputs.desc: Map of prediction errors at holdout locations

process: Extract predicted values at each holdout location.
Compute error metrics (RMSE, MAE, R-squared, mean bias).
Map the residuals to check for spatial patterns in the errors.
Flag regions where prediction error exceeds an acceptable threshold.

steps.description: Compile the geospatial analysis into a report with maps, autocorrelation results, interpolation surfaces, hotspot maps, and validation summary.

outputs.name: spatial-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete geospatial analysis report with maps and statistics

outputs.name: spatial-figures
outputs.desc: All maps and plots from the analysis

process: Assemble the choropleth, interpolation, and hotspot maps.
Write the methods narrative covering CRS, interpolation, and hotspot detection.
Summarize validation results and autocorrelation findings.
Compile all elements into the final report.

description: Model a dose-response relationship from raw data through curve plotting, model selection, parameter estimation, confidence intervals, and threshold testing.

steps.description: Organize dose and response data, check for outliers, and prepare the dataset for modeling.

inputs.name: raw-dose-response-data
inputs.desc: Table of dose levels and corresponding response measurements

outputs.name: cleaned-data
outputs.desc: Validated dose-response dataset with outliers flagged

outputs.name: data-summary
outputs.desc: Dose levels, replicates per dose, response range, and outlier report

process: Import the raw data and verify dose and response columns.
Check for missing values and flag statistical outliers (Grubbs or IQR).
Summarize the number of replicates at each dose level.
Report the response range and any data quality issues.

steps.description: Plot the raw dose-response data with error bars and visually inspect the shape of the relationship.

inputs.name: x-axis-scale
inputs.desc: Linear or log scale for dose axis

outputs.name: raw-curve-plot
outputs.desc: Scatter plot of dose vs. response with error bars

outputs.name: shape-assessment
outputs.desc: Visual assessment of monotonicity, saturation, and potential threshold

process: Plot individual data points and group means with standard error bars.
Display on both linear and log-dose scales.
Annotate apparent features (plateau, inflection point, threshold region).
Record the visual shape assessment to guide model selection.

steps.description: Evaluate candidate dose-response models and select the best fit using information criteria and residual diagnostics.

inputs.name: shape-assessment
inputs.desc: Visual assessment from the curve plot

outputs.name: selected-dr-model
outputs.desc: Best-fit model type with initial parameter estimates

outputs.name: model-comparison
outputs.desc: AIC, BIC, and residual diagnostics for each candidate

process: Define candidate models (4-parameter logistic, Hill, linear-quadratic, probit).
Fit each candidate to the data using nonlinear least squares or maximum likelihood.
Compare by AIC, BIC, and residual patterns.
Select the model with the best balance of fit and parsimony.

steps.description: Estimate key pharmacological or toxicological parameters (EC50, LD50, NOAEL, BMD) from the fitted model with confidence intervals.

outputs.name: parameter-estimates
outputs.desc: EC50/LD50/NOAEL/BMD with 95% confidence intervals

outputs.name: fitted-curve
outputs.desc: Smooth fitted curve overlaid on data points

process: Compute point estimates for EC50, LD50, or the relevant potency metric.
Estimate NOAEL from the last dose without significant effect.
Compute benchmark dose (BMD) and its lower confidence limit (BMDL).
Generate the fitted curve with confidence band for the report.

steps.description: Test whether the dose-response data show hormesis (low-dose stimulation) or a threshold below which no effect occurs.

inputs.name: parameter-estimates
inputs.desc: Fitted model parameters and potency metrics

outputs.name: threshold-test-results
outputs.desc: Statistical test results for hormesis and threshold hypotheses

outputs.name: threshold-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated threshold dose if supported, or null if not

process: Test low-dose groups against control using Dunnett's or Williams' test.
Fit a hormetic model (Brain-Cousens or Cedergreen-Ritz-Streibig) and compare to monotone.
If hormesis is not supported, test for a threshold using segmented regression.
Report the test statistics, p-values, and conclusion.

steps.description: Produce the dose-response analysis report with fitted curves, parameter table, threshold test results, and methods description.

outputs.name: dose-response-report
outputs.desc: Complete dose-response analysis report

outputs.name: dose-response-figures
outputs.desc: Fitted curve plot, residual plot, and threshold test plot

process: Generate the fitted curve figure with data points, confidence band, and parameter annotations.
Build the parameter summary table.
Write the methods section covering model selection, fitting, and threshold testing.
Compile figures, tables, and narrative into the final report.

description: Analyze time-to-event data through censoring definition, Kaplan-Meier estimation, log-rank testing, Cox regression, assumption checking, and prognostic factor identification.

steps.description: Define the event of interest, censoring rules, and time origin for survival analysis.

inputs.name: study-data
inputs.desc: Patient or subject-level data with dates and outcomes

inputs.name: event-definition
inputs.desc: What constitutes the event (death, relapse, failure)

outputs.name: survival-dataset
outputs.desc: Dataset with time, event indicator, and covariates for each subject

outputs.name: censoring-summary
outputs.desc: Proportion censored, follow-up time distribution, and event count

process: Define the event, censoring conditions (lost to follow-up, study end, competing event).
Compute the survival time from the origin to event or censoring date.
Create the binary event indicator.
Summarize median follow-up, event rate, and censoring proportion.

steps.description: Construct Kaplan-Meier survival curves for each group and estimate median survival times.

inputs.name: survival-dataset
inputs.desc: Time, event indicator, and group variable

inputs.name: grouping-variable
inputs.desc: Variable defining comparison groups (treatment vs. control)

outputs.name: km-curves
outputs.desc: Kaplan-Meier survival curves with 95% confidence intervals for each group

outputs.name: km-estimates
outputs.desc: Median survival, 1-year and 5-year survival rates per group

process: Compute the Kaplan-Meier estimator for each group.
Calculate the Greenwood confidence intervals at each event time.
Estimate median survival and landmark survival rates.
Plot the survival curves with number-at-risk table.

steps.description: Test whether survival curves differ significantly between groups using the log-rank test and variants.

inputs.name: survival-dataset
inputs.desc: Time, event indicator, and group variable

outputs.name: logrank-result
outputs.desc: Log-rank chi-squared, degrees of freedom, and p-value

outputs.name: test-variants
outputs.desc: Wilcoxon (Breslow) and Tarone-Ware test results for comparison

process: Compute the log-rank test statistic comparing observed vs. expected events per group.
Compute the Wilcoxon variant (weights early events more) and Tarone-Ware variant.
Report chi-squared statistics and p-values for each test.
Note whether the tests agree or suggest different timing of group divergence.

steps.description: Fit a Cox proportional hazards model with covariates and report hazard ratios.

inputs.name: survival-dataset
inputs.desc: Time, event indicator, and covariate columns

inputs.name: covariate-list
inputs.desc: List of covariates to include in the model

outputs.name: cox-model
outputs.desc: Fitted Cox model with hazard ratios, confidence intervals, and p-values

outputs.name: cox-summary
outputs.desc: Model concordance, likelihood ratio test, and covariate effect table

process: Fit the Cox proportional hazards model using partial likelihood.
Compute hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals for each covariate.
Report the concordance index (C-statistic) for discrimination.
Perform the likelihood ratio test for overall model significance.

steps.description: Verify the proportional hazards assumption using Schoenfeld residuals and log-log plots.

outputs.name: ph-test-results
outputs.desc: Schoenfeld residual test p-values for each covariate and global test

outputs.name: diagnostic-plots
outputs.desc: Schoenfeld residual plots and log-log survival plots

process: Compute scaled Schoenfeld residuals for each covariate.
Test the correlation of residuals with time (Grambsch-Therneau test).
Generate log-log survival plots for categorical covariates.
Identify covariates that violate the assumption and suggest remedies (stratification or time interaction).

steps.description: Identify the most important prognostic factors through variable selection and effect size ranking.

inputs.name: cox-model
inputs.desc: Fitted Cox model with all candidate covariates

outputs.name: prognostic-factors
outputs.desc: Ranked list of significant prognostic factors with hazard ratios

outputs.name: forest-plot
outputs.desc: Forest plot of hazard ratios with confidence intervals

process: Apply stepwise or penalized selection (LASSO) to identify significant factors.
Rank factors by the magnitude of the hazard ratio.
Generate the forest plot for visual comparison.
Report the final parsimonious model with its concordance.

steps.description: Produce the survival analysis report with KM curves, Cox results, assumption diagnostics, and forest plot.

outputs.name: survival-report
outputs.desc: Complete survival analysis report

outputs.name: survival-figures
outputs.desc: KM curves, forest plot, and diagnostic plots

process: Assemble all figures (KM curves, forest plot, Schoenfeld plots).
Write the results narrative covering group comparisons and prognostic factors.
Describe the methods including event definition, censoring, and model specification.
Compile the final report.

description: Analyze stable or radiogenic isotope ratios from sample preparation through mass spectrometry measurement, fractionation correction, standard comparison, contextual interpretation, and precision assessment.

steps.description: Prepare samples for isotope ratio measurement: dissolution, chemical separation, or combustion as needed.

inputs.name: sample-material
inputs.desc: Description of the material (rock, bone, water, organic tissue)

inputs.name: isotope-system
inputs.desc: Which isotope system (C, N, O, S, Sr, Pb, U-Th)

outputs.name: prepared-samples
outputs.desc: Samples ready for mass spectrometer loading

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Reagents, blanks, procedural losses, and contamination controls

process: Select the preparation protocol for the isotope system and sample type.
Process samples alongside procedural blanks and reference materials.
Quantify recovery and check for contamination at each step.
Log all reagent lots, temperatures, and timing.

steps.description: Measure isotope ratios on the mass spectrometer with bracketing standards and replicate analyses.

inputs.name: measurement-protocol
inputs.desc: Instrument settings, integration time, and standard bracketing scheme

outputs.name: raw-ratios
outputs.desc: Measured isotope ratios for each sample and standard run

outputs.name: instrument-log
outputs.desc: Run sequence, signal intensity, and stability metrics

process: Tune the mass spectrometer and verify performance on a check standard.
Run samples in the standard-sample-standard bracketing sequence.
Record raw ratio, signal intensity, and internal precision for each measurement.
Flag runs with low signal, drift, or interference.

steps.description: Correct raw isotope ratios for instrumental mass fractionation, isobaric interferences, and blank contributions.

outputs.name: corrected-ratios
outputs.desc: Ratios after fractionation, interference, and blank corrections

outputs.name: correction-log
outputs.desc: Magnitude of each correction applied to each sample

process: Apply mass bias correction using the bracketing standards or internal normalization.
Subtract isobaric interference contributions (e.g., Rb on Sr, Hg on Pb).
Subtract the procedural blank contribution.
Propagate uncertainties through each correction.

steps.description: Express corrected ratios in delta notation relative to international standards and verify accuracy against reference materials.

inputs.name: reference-standard
inputs.desc: International standard (VPDB, VSMOW, AIR, CDT, NBS-987)

outputs.name: delta-values
outputs.desc: Isotope ratios expressed as delta per mil relative to the standard

outputs.name: accuracy-check
outputs.desc: Reference material results compared to accepted values

process: Convert corrected ratios to delta notation using the reference standard.
Compare measured reference material values to their accepted values.
Flag any reference material result outside 2 standard deviations of the accepted value.
Report overall analytical accuracy.

steps.description: Interpret isotope values in the appropriate context: provenance, diet reconstruction, paleothermometry, or geochronology.

inputs.name: delta-values
inputs.desc: Sample isotope values in delta notation

inputs.name: interpretive-framework
inputs.desc: Which context applies (provenance, paleoecology, temperature, age)

outputs.name: interpretation
outputs.desc: Narrative interpretation of the isotope data in the selected context

outputs.name: comparison-dataset
outputs.desc: Sample values plotted against published reference ranges

process: Compile published reference data for the relevant context.
Plot sample values against the reference ranges.
Identify which reference group each sample falls within.
Write the interpretive narrative with caveats about mixing and diagenesis.

steps.description: Quantify analytical precision from replicate measurements and propagate uncertainty to final interpretations.

inputs.name: delta-values
inputs.desc: All sample and replicate delta values

outputs.name: precision-report
outputs.desc: Internal and external precision, reproducibility, and total uncertainty budget

outputs.name: uncertainty-budget
outputs.desc: Breakdown of uncertainty contributions from measurement, correction, and blank

process: Compute internal precision from within-run replicates.
Compute external precision from between-session replicates of reference materials.
Build the uncertainty budget showing the contribution of each error source.
Report the total combined uncertainty for each sample.

steps.description: Produce the isotope analysis report with data tables, comparison plots, precision summary, and methods.

outputs.name: isotope-report
outputs.desc: Complete isotope ratio analysis report

outputs.name: isotope-figures
outputs.desc: Delta value plots, comparison charts, and uncertainty diagrams

process: Build the data table with sample ID, delta values, and uncertainties.
Generate comparison plots and uncertainty diagrams.
Write the methods section covering preparation, measurement, and correction.
Compile the final report.

description: Quantify features in scientific images through preprocessing, segmentation, morphometric extraction, classification, summary statistics, and annotation validation.

steps.description: Preprocess scientific images with noise reduction, contrast adjustment, and background correction.

inputs.name: raw-images
inputs.desc: Set of raw scientific images (microscopy, satellite, medical)

inputs.name: preprocessing-params
inputs.desc: Filter type, kernel size, contrast method

outputs.name: preprocessed-images
outputs.desc: Cleaned images ready for segmentation

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Filters applied, before/after metrics, and rejected images

process: Apply noise reduction (Gaussian, median, or non-local means) to each image.
Correct uneven illumination or background gradient.
Adjust contrast using histogram equalization or CLAHE.
Log all parameters and flag images that remain below quality threshold.

steps.description: Segment regions of interest in the preprocessed images using thresholding, watershed, or machine learning methods.

inputs.name: segmentation-method
inputs.desc: Otsu threshold, watershed, U-Net, or manual seeds

outputs.name: segmented-masks
outputs.desc: Binary or labeled masks identifying each region of interest

outputs.name: segmentation-stats
outputs.desc: Object count, coverage fraction, and segmentation confidence per image

process: Apply the chosen segmentation algorithm.
Post-process masks (fill holes, remove small objects, split touching objects).
Label each connected region with a unique ID.
Report object count and coverage fraction for each image.

steps.description: Measure shape and size features for each segmented object: area, perimeter, circularity, aspect ratio, and intensity statistics.

inputs.name: preprocessed-images
inputs.desc: Original intensity images for intensity measurements

outputs.name: morphometric-table
outputs.desc: Table of measurements for each object (area, perimeter, circularity, intensity)

outputs.name: measurement-distributions
outputs.desc: Histograms and summary statistics for each measured feature

process: Compute geometric features (area, perimeter, major/minor axis, circularity, solidity) for each object.
Extract intensity statistics (mean, median, standard deviation) within each object mask.
Compute derived features (aspect ratio, form factor, optical density).
Build the per-object measurement table.

steps.description: Classify segmented objects into categories based on their morphometric and intensity features.

inputs.name: classification-scheme
inputs.desc: Categories and criteria (rule-based thresholds or trained classifier)

outputs.name: classified-objects
outputs.desc: Each object assigned to a category with confidence score

outputs.name: classification-summary
outputs.desc: Count and proportion per category, confusion matrix if ground truth available

process: Apply the classification rules or trained model to each object's feature vector.
Assign each object to a category with a confidence score.
Tabulate counts and proportions per category.
If ground truth labels exist, compute the confusion matrix and accuracy metrics.

steps.description: Compute summary statistics across the entire image set: per-image and per-group means, variance, and comparisons.

inputs.name: experimental-groups
inputs.desc: Which images belong to which experimental condition

outputs.name: group-statistics
outputs.desc: Per-group summary (means, SDs, medians) for each measured feature

outputs.name: group-comparison
outputs.desc: Statistical test results comparing groups (t-test, ANOVA, or nonparametric)

process: Aggregate object-level measurements to per-image summaries.
Compute group-level means, standard deviations, and medians.
Test for group differences using appropriate statistical tests.
Report effect sizes and confidence intervals alongside p-values.

steps.description: Validate automated segmentation and classification against manual expert annotations on a subset of images.

inputs.name: manual-annotations
inputs.desc: Expert-drawn annotations on a validation subset

outputs.name: validation-scores
outputs.desc: Dice coefficient, IoU, precision, recall, and F1 for segmentation and classification

outputs.name: error-examples
outputs.desc: Gallery of cases where automation disagreed most with the expert

process: Match automated objects to manual annotations by overlap.
Compute pixel-level Dice coefficient and IoU.
Compute object-level precision, recall, and F1.
Extract the top disagreement cases for visual review.

steps.description: Produce the image quantification report with representative images, measurement distributions, group comparisons, and validation scores.

outputs.name: quantification-report
outputs.desc: Complete image analysis report with figures and tables

outputs.name: quantification-figures
outputs.desc: Representative images, measurement plots, and comparison charts

process: Select representative images showing segmentation overlays.
Generate measurement distribution plots and group comparison charts.
Write the methods covering preprocessing, segmentation, and classification.
Compile the final report with all figures, tables, and validation summary.

description: Test how sensitive a model's output is to its inputs through parameter identification, method selection, range definition, analysis execution, influence ranking, and interaction detection.

steps.description: Catalog all model parameters, their physical meaning, nominal values, and plausible ranges.

inputs.name: model-description
inputs.desc: Documentation or code of the model to analyze

inputs.name: domain-knowledge
inputs.desc: Literature or expert input on parameter bounds

outputs.name: parameter-catalog
outputs.desc: Table of all parameters with name, nominal value, unit, and plausible range

outputs.name: parameter-count
outputs.desc: Total number of parameters and their grouping by subsystem

process: List every adjustable parameter in the model.
Record the nominal (baseline) value and physical unit for each.
Assign plausible minimum and maximum values from literature or expert judgment.
Group parameters by model subsystem for organized reporting.

steps.description: Choose the sensitivity analysis method based on the number of parameters, computational cost, and whether interactions matter.

inputs.name: computational-budget
inputs.desc: Maximum number of model evaluations feasible

outputs.name: selected-sa-method
outputs.desc: Chosen method (OAT, Morris, Sobol, FAST, or PAWN) with justification

outputs.name: sample-design
outputs.desc: Number of samples, sampling scheme, and expected model runs

process: Estimate the number of model runs each candidate method requires.
Assess whether parameter interactions are expected or important.
Select the method that fits within the computational budget while answering the question.
Design the sampling scheme (Latin hypercube, Saltelli, or Morris trajectories).

steps.description: Define probability distributions or ranges for each parameter to sample during the sensitivity analysis.

outputs.name: parameter-distributions
outputs.desc: Distribution type and parameters for each model parameter

outputs.name: sample-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of parameter combinations to evaluate

process: Assign a distribution to each parameter (uniform, normal, log-normal, or triangular).
Generate the sample matrix using the method's sampling scheme.
Verify the sample matrix covers the defined ranges adequately.
Check for correlations between parameters that need to be preserved.

steps.description: Execute the model at each sample point and collect the output of interest.

outputs.name: model-outputs
outputs.desc: Output value(s) at each sample point

outputs.name: run-log
outputs.desc: Completion status, runtime, and any failed evaluations

process: Set up the model runner with each parameter combination from the sample matrix.
Execute all model runs (parallelized where possible).
Collect the output of interest from each run.
Log any failed runs and decide whether to resample or exclude.

steps.description: Compute sensitivity indices and rank parameters by their influence on the model output.

inputs.name: model-outputs
inputs.desc: Output values from all sample points

outputs.name: sensitivity-indices
outputs.desc: First-order and total-effect indices (or Morris mu* and sigma) for each parameter

outputs.name: influence-ranking
outputs.desc: Parameters ranked from most to least influential

process: Compute the method-specific sensitivity indices for each parameter.
Rank parameters by their first-order (or mu*) index.
Identify parameters with negligible influence that could be fixed at nominal values.
Report the total variance explained by first-order effects vs. interactions.

steps.description: Identify and quantify interaction effects between parameters that jointly influence the output.

inputs.name: model-outputs
inputs.desc: Full output dataset from sample runs

outputs.name: interaction-pairs
outputs.desc: Parameter pairs with significant interaction effects and their second-order indices

outputs.name: interaction-plots
outputs.desc: Scatter or heatmap plots showing the joint effect of interacting parameter pairs

process: Compute second-order Sobol indices for parameter pairs (or infer interactions from total minus first-order gap).
Identify pairs where the interaction index exceeds a threshold.
Generate joint-effect plots for the top interacting pairs.
Summarize the fraction of output variance due to interactions.

steps.description: Produce the sensitivity analysis report with parameter rankings, interaction findings, and recommendations for model refinement.

outputs.name: sensitivity-report
outputs.desc: Complete sensitivity analysis report

outputs.name: sensitivity-figures
outputs.desc: Tornado plot, scatter plots, and interaction heatmaps

process: Generate the tornado plot of first-order sensitivity indices.
Include scatter plots and heatmaps for the top interactions.
Write the methods section covering the SA method, sampling, and index computation.
Compile findings and recommendations for which parameters to measure more precisely.

description: Prepare a scientific manuscript for peer review through results organization, methods writing, supplementary preparation, reference formatting, cover letter drafting, and journal criteria self-review.

steps.description: Organize raw results into a logical narrative: choose the order of findings, pair each with the right figure or table, and write the results text.

inputs.name: raw-results
inputs.desc: All analysis outputs, figures, and tables from the study

inputs.name: study-questions
inputs.desc: The research questions or hypotheses being addressed

outputs.name: results-draft
outputs.desc: Structured results section with figure and table references

outputs.name: figure-table-list
outputs.desc: Ordered list of figures and tables with captions

process: Group results by the research question they address.
Order findings from most central to supporting or exploratory.
Write the results text, stating what each figure or table shows without interpreting.
Check that every figure and table is referenced in the text.

steps.description: Write the methods section with enough detail for another researcher to replicate the study.

inputs.name: study-protocol
inputs.desc: The actual procedures, materials, and instruments used

outputs.name: methods-draft
outputs.desc: Methods section organized by study design, materials, procedures, and analysis

outputs.name: replication-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of details needed for replication (reagent catalog numbers, software versions, parameters)

process: Organize methods into subsections: study design, participants/samples, materials, procedures, and analysis.
Include specific quantities, catalog numbers, software versions, and parameter settings.
Describe the statistical analysis plan including tests, corrections, and significance threshold.
Check against the replication checklist to ensure nothing is omitted.

steps.description: Compile supplementary materials: additional figures, extended tables, raw data summaries, and code availability statements.

inputs.name: raw-results
inputs.desc: Full set of results including those not in the main text

outputs.name: supplementary-package
outputs.desc: Organized supplementary files with index

outputs.name: data-availability-statement
outputs.desc: Statement describing where data and code can be accessed

process: Identify results that support the main findings but do not fit in the main text.
Format supplementary figures and tables with captions and numbering.
Prepare the code availability or repository link.
Write the data availability statement per the target journal's policy.

steps.description: Format all in-text citations and the reference list according to the target journal's style.

inputs.name: manuscript-draft
inputs.desc: Combined manuscript text with informal citations

inputs.name: target-journal-style
inputs.desc: Citation style name or journal formatting guide

outputs.name: formatted-references
outputs.desc: Reference list in the correct journal style

outputs.name: citation-check
outputs.desc: Report of any missing references, duplicates, or uncited entries

process: Parse all in-text citations from the manuscript.
Match each citation to a reference entry.
Format each reference according to the target style (author-date, numbered, Vancouver).
Report any citations without a reference or references never cited.

steps.description: Draft the cover letter to the journal editor explaining the significance of the work and why it fits the journal's scope.

inputs.name: target-journal-scope
inputs.desc: The journal's aims and scope statement

outputs.name: cover-letter
outputs.desc: Cover letter addressed to the editor

outputs.name: suggested-reviewers
outputs.desc: List of 3-5 suggested peer reviewers with justification

process: State the main finding in one sentence.
Explain why this finding fits the journal's scope and audience.
Note any conflicts of interest or prior preprint posting.
Suggest qualified reviewers who are not collaborators.

steps.description: Complete the journal's author checklist covering ethics, data sharing, formatting, and reporting standards.

inputs.name: journal-checklist
inputs.desc: The target journal's submission checklist or reporting guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA)

outputs.name: completed-checklist
outputs.desc: Filled-in author checklist with page/section references

outputs.name: compliance-gaps
outputs.desc: Any checklist items not yet addressed in the manuscript

process: Map each checklist item to the corresponding section of the manuscript.
Fill in page numbers or section references for each item.
Flag any items that cannot be satisfied and note the reason.
List compliance gaps that need to be fixed before submission.

steps.description: Self-review the manuscript against the target journal's criteria: scope fit, novelty, statistical rigor, figure quality, and word count.

inputs.name: target-journal-scope
inputs.desc: Journal aims, scope, and formatting requirements

outputs.name: self-review-report
outputs.desc: Assessment of manuscript readiness with specific issues to fix

outputs.name: submission-package
outputs.desc: Final list of files to submit: manuscript, figures, supplementary, cover letter, checklist

process: Check word count, figure count, and reference count against journal limits.
Verify figure resolution and format meet the journal's requirements.
Assess whether the abstract, title, and keywords match the journal's conventions.
Compile the final submission package file list.

description: Archive research data for long-term access through inventory, persistent identification, metadata writing, repository selection, packaging, and deposit verification.

steps.description: Catalog all datasets, code, and supporting files produced by the research, noting formats, sizes, and sensitivity.

inputs.name: project-files
inputs.desc: Root directory or listing of all research outputs

inputs.name: sensitivity-classification
inputs.desc: Rules for identifying restricted or embargoed data

outputs.name: file-inventory
outputs.desc: Table of every file with path, format, size, description, and sensitivity flag

outputs.name: inventory-summary
outputs.desc: Total file count, size, format distribution, and restricted file count

process: Walk the project directory and record each file's path, format, and size.
Write a one-line description for each file or group of files.
Flag files containing personal, proprietary, or embargoed data.
Summarize totals by format and sensitivity level.

steps.description: Reserve persistent identifiers (DOIs) for datasets and link them to the manuscript DOI.

inputs.name: file-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of files to be deposited

inputs.name: manuscript-doi
inputs.desc: DOI of the associated publication if available

outputs.name: doi-assignments
outputs.desc: DOI reserved for each dataset or dataset collection

outputs.name: linkage-record
outputs.desc: Mapping between dataset DOIs and the manuscript DOI

process: Decide the granularity of DOI assignment (one per dataset, one per collection, or one per version).
Reserve DOIs through the repository's registration service (DataCite).
Record the bidirectional link between dataset and manuscript DOIs.
Verify that reserved DOIs resolve to the expected landing page.

steps.description: Write structured metadata following a standard schema (Dublin Core, DataCite, or domain-specific) for each dataset.

inputs.name: metadata-standard
inputs.desc: Which schema to follow (Dublin Core, DataCite, DDI, EML)

outputs.name: metadata-records
outputs.desc: Structured metadata file for each dataset

outputs.name: metadata-validation
outputs.desc: Validation report confirming compliance with the chosen schema

process: Fill in required fields: title, creator, date, description, subject, format, rights.
Add recommended fields: spatial coverage, temporal coverage, methodology, funding.
Validate each record against the schema.
Fix any validation errors and re-check.

steps.description: Choose the appropriate data repository based on the domain, funder requirements, and data sensitivity.

inputs.name: inventory-summary
inputs.desc: Summary of data types, sizes, and sensitivity

inputs.name: funder-requirements
inputs.desc: Funder's data sharing policy and preferred repositories

outputs.name: selected-repository
outputs.desc: Chosen repository with deposit URL and submission guide link

outputs.name: repository-rationale
outputs.desc: Why this repository fits the data type, funder, and access needs

process: List candidate repositories (domain-specific like GenBank, Dryad, Zenodo, or institutional).
Check each against funder mandates and data type compatibility.
Verify size limits, embargo support, and access control options.
Select the best fit and document the rationale.

steps.description: Package the data files with metadata, README, and data dictionary into the repository's required submission format.

outputs.name: submission-package
outputs.desc: Packaged archive(s) ready for upload

outputs.name: package-manifest
outputs.desc: Checksum manifest for integrity verification

process: Organize files into the repository's expected directory structure.
Include the metadata records and README at the top level.
Compute checksums (MD5 or SHA-256) for every file.
Create the archive in the required format (zip, tar.gz, or BagIt).

steps.description: Generate a data dictionary describing every variable in every dataset: name, type, unit, allowed values, and meaning.

inputs.name: project-files
inputs.desc: The actual data files to inspect

outputs.name: data-dictionary
outputs.desc: Table of all variables across all datasets with full descriptions

outputs.name: readme-file
outputs.desc: Human-readable README summarizing the data collection and file structure

process: For each tabular dataset, list every column with name, data type, unit, and description.
For each non-tabular file, describe the content and format.
Write the README covering the study context, methods summary, and file relationships.
Cross-reference the data dictionary with the metadata records for consistency.

steps.description: Upload the package to the repository, verify the deposit, and confirm that the DOI resolves and metadata displays correctly.

outputs.name: deposit-confirmation
outputs.desc: Repository receipt with accession number and permanent URL

outputs.name: verification-report
outputs.desc: Confirmation that DOI resolves, files download, checksums match, and metadata renders

process: Upload the package to the selected repository.
Verify the DOI resolves to the landing page with correct metadata.
Download a file and verify its checksum against the manifest.
Confirm embargo or access restrictions are correctly applied.
